object.title: Li's conjecture on generalized connectivity of complete multipartite graphs
object.statement: Let $G$ be a complete multipartite graph, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $S$ be a $k$-subset of $V(G)$. **Li's conjecture.** We have $\kappa_k(G)=\kappa(S)$ when the numbers of vertices in the parts of $G$ that are not in $S$ are almost the same. The conjecture generalizes the preceding complete equipartite formulation; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Xueliang Li and Yaping Mao, “A survey on the generalized connectivity of graphs”, arXiv:1207.1838 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.1838

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2012).

object.title: PSpace-completeness conjecture for Pirates and Treasure
object.statement: Consider the decision problem Pirates and Treasure, whose input is a graph $G$ and whose outcome is determined by the game's scoring-play rules. **PSpace-completeness conjecture.** Pirates and Treasure is PSpace-complete. The problem is stated to lie in PSpace, while its membership in NP is considered unlikely; the source gives no resolution of PSpace-hardness or PSpace-completeness.
object.source_name: Fraser Stewart, “Pirates and Treasure”, arXiv:1208.2432 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.2432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2012).

object.title: Bridgeless-core conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let a **core** be a core associated with three 1-factors of $G$. **Bridgeless-core conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a bridgeless core.

The claim is proposed as the converse of the elementary implication that a cubic graph with a bridge has a bridge in every core. The source gives no resolution status.
object.source_name: Eckhard Steffen, “1-factor and cycle covers of cubic graphs”, arXiv:1209.4510 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4510

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2012). “The first conjecture is disproved by Kochol and the second is still open.”

object.title: The classification conjecture for quasi-constant $c_2$-invariants
object.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a completed primitive graph, let $c_2[\Gamma]_q$ denote its $c_2$-invariant, and call $\Gamma$ **quasi-constant** when this invariant is one of the quasi-constant functions described in the source; let $z_2$, $z_3$, and $z_4$ denote the corresponding functions in the source. The **classification conjecture for quasi-constant $c_2$-invariants** states that if $\Gamma$ is quasi-constant, then its $c_2$-invariant is $0$, $-1$, $-z_2$, $-z_3$, or $-z_4$. Moreover, if

$$
c_2[\Gamma]_q\equiv -1\pmod q,
$$

then the ancestor of $\Gamma$ is $K_5$. This conjecture is based on data through loop order $10$ and organizes primitive $\phi^4$ graphs into weight-drop graphs, graphs with non-polynomial point counts, and the family whose ancestor is $K_5$; the source presents it as conjectural.
object.source_name: Francis Brown and Oliver Schnetz, “Modular forms in Quantum Field Theory”, arXiv:1304.5342 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5342

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2013). “Although the conjecture is true for small graphs and for certain sets of nearly complete graphs , , it is false in general.”

object.title: Diagram matroid basis-count conjecture
object.statement:
Let $w\in S_n$, and let $DM_w$ be the diagram matroid of $w$, obtained from a generic matrix $[A\mid I_n]$ whose entries satisfy $A_{ij}=0$ whenever $(i,j)\in D(w)$, where

$$
D(w)=\{(i,w(j))\in[n]\times[n]:i<j,\ w(i)>w(j)\}.
$$

For a permutation $v$, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k$ be the lengths of the runs of anti-fixed points of $v$, and write $C_m$ for the $m$th Catalan number. **Diagram matroid basis-count conjecture.** For any $w\in S_n$, the number of bases of $DM_w$ is

$$
\sum_{\substack{v\geq w\\text{$v$ avoids $123$}}}C_{\ell_1+1}\cdots C_{\ell_k+1}.
$$

This extends the corresponding basis-count formula to diagram matroids. The source indicates that a proof might be obtained by Möbius inversion, but that a more substantial sign-reversing involution is needed; the conjecture is not reported as resolved.
object.source_name: Brendan Pawlowski, “Catalan matroid decompositions of certain positroids”, arXiv:1502.00158 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.00158

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2015). “This conjecture has been verified through $S_7$.”

329796.object_hash_serialization: UTF8 JSON ensure_ascii=False sort_keys=True separators comma/colon

object.title: Monotonicity conjecture for avoiding increasing patterns in the Mallows distribution
object.statement:
Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $P_n(12\dots m,q)$ denote the probability that a permutation of size $n$ drawn from the Mallows distribution with parameter $q>0$ avoids the increasing pattern $12\dots m$. Let $\rho(12\dots m,q)$ denote the corresponding growth rate of the pattern-avoidance probability. **Monotonicity conjecture.** If $q<q'$, then

$$
P_n(12\dots m,q)<P_n(12\dots m,q')
$$

and

$$
\rho(12\dots m,q)<\rho(12\dots m,q').
$$

Increasing $q$ gives higher probability to permutations with more inversions, so the conjecture asserts that avoiding an increasing pattern becomes more likely, both at finite size and at the level of growth rates. It is supported by the numerical evidence described in the source, but the authors were unable to establish it using their available techniques and leave it as an open problem.
object.source_name: Harry Crane, Stephen DeSalvo and Sergi Elizalde, “The probability of avoiding consecutive patterns in the Mallows distribution”, arXiv:1609.01370 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.01370

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2016). “We have been unable to establish the conjecture using either of these techniques, and so we leave this as an open problem.”

object.title: Monoidality conjecture for the shape functor of constructible polygraphs
object.statement: Let $\mathbf{CPol}$ be the category of constructible polygraphs, with monoidal structures given by the lax Gray product $\scaleobj{0.75}{\boxtimes}$ and the join $\star$, and let $\omega\mathbf{Cat}$ be the category of $\omega$-categories with the corresponding monoidal structures. The shape functor is denoted by $-_{\omega}:\mathbf{CPol}\to\omega\mathbf{Cat}$. **Monoidality conjecture.** The functor $-_{\omega}$ is monoidal both from $(\mathbf{CPol},\,\scaleobj{0.75}{\boxtimes},1)$ to $(\omega\mathbf{Cat},\,\scaleobj{0.75}{\boxtimes},1)$ and from $(\mathbf{CPol},\,\star,\emptyset)$ to $(\omega\mathbf{Cat},\,\star,\emptyset)$. This would show that the combinatorial shape construction preserves both fundamental monoidal structures relevant to higher categories; the source presents it as an expected result, with no proof or resolution supplied.
object.source_name: Amar Hadzihasanovic, “A combinatorial-topological shape category for polygraphs”, arXiv:1806.10353 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.10353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2018).

object.title: The shadow-doubling conjecture for 3-wise intersecting families
object.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $2^{[n]}$ denote the family of all subsets of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal F\subset 2^{[n]}$. Define the immediate shadow by

$$
\partial\mathcal F:=\{G:\exists F\in\mathcal F,\ G\subset F,\ |F\setminus G|=1\},
$$

and set $\sigma(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F\cup\partial\mathcal F$. A family is $3$-wise intersecting if every three members have nonempty intersection. **Shadow-doubling conjecture.** If $\mathcal F$ is $3$-wise intersecting, then

$$
|\sigma(\mathcal F)|\ge 2|\mathcal F|.
$$

The conjecture asks for a lower bound on the size of a family together with its immediate shadow. In the supplied text, the preceding discussion establishes a different result with the constant $38$ for a stronger intersection condition, but gives no resolution of this shadow inequality; it therefore remains open.
object.source_name: Peter Frankl and Andrey Kupavskii, “Incompatible intersection properties”, arXiv:1808.01229 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.01229

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

object.title: Last-entry and right-to-left-maximum equidistribution for 2314-avoiding permutations
object.statement:
Let $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ be the permutations avoiding the vincular pattern $\underline{23}14$, and let $cmathbf{I}_n(\underline{12}0)$ be the inversion sequences avoiding $\underline{12}0$. For a permutation or inversion sequence, let $cmathrm{last}$ denote its last entry. Let $cmathrm{rmax}$ denote the number of right-to-left maxima of a permutation and $cmathrm{rmin}$ the number of right-to-left minima of an inversion sequence.
**Last-entry equidistribution conjecture.** The pair $(\operatorname{last},\operatorname{rmax})$ on $cmathfrak{S}_n(\underline{23}14)$ has the same distribution as $(\operatorname{last},\operatorname{rmin})$ on $cmathbf{I}_n(\underline{12}0)$.
This is another refinement of the powered-Catalan enumeration conjecture for $\underline{23}14$-avoiding permutations, using the last-entry statistic together with an extremal-entry statistic.
object.source_name: Zhicong Lin and Shishuo Fu, “On 120-avoiding inversion and ascent sequences”, arXiv:2003.11813 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.11813

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2020).

object.title: The permutation-orbifold isomorphism for the principal mathfrak{f}_4 affine W-algebra
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}_{-22/5}$ be the simple Virasoro vertex algebra of central charge $-22/5$, and let $S_4$ act on its fourth tensor power by permuting the tensor factors. Write $\mathcal{W}_{-49/6}(\mathfrak{f}_4,f_{\mathrm{princ}})$ for the affine W-algebra at level $-49/6$ associated with the principal nilpotent element of the simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{f}_4$. **Permutation-orbifold isomorphism.** We have an isomorphism of vertex algebras

$$
(\mathcal{L}_{-22/5}^{\otimes 4})^{S_4} \cong \mathcal{W}_{-49/6}(\mathfrak{f}_4,f_{\mathrm{princ}}).
$$

This is presented as a related conjecture beyond the authors' reach, extending the preceding established permutation-orbifold identification to an affine W-algebra outside the usual rational series. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Antun Milas, Michael Penn and Christopher Sadowski, “Permutation orbifolds of Virasoro vertex algebras and W-algebras”, arXiv:2005.08398 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08398

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

object.title: Flandrin et al.'s spanning-tree branch-vertex conjecture
object.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$. **Flandrin et al.'s conjecture.** If

$$
\sigma_{k+3}(G)\geq n-k,
$$

then $G$ has a spanning tree with at most $k$ branch vertices. This conjecture proposes a sufficient degree-sum condition for a connected graph to have a spanning tree with a bounded number of branch vertices; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
object.source_name: Pham Hoang Ha, “Spanning trees of K_1,4-free graphs with a bounded number of leaves and branch vertices”, arXiv:2201.01043 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.01043

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: Algebraic lower-bound conjecture for the complement connectivity pair
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with complement $G^c$, and write

$$
x=\lambda_2(G),\qquad y=\lambda_2(G^c).
$$

Assume that $x<1$ and $y<1$.

**Algebraic lower-bound conjecture.** The pair $(x,y)$ satisfies

$$
xy(2-xy)\geq n(1-x)(1-y)(n-2-x-y),
$$

with equality only when $G$ belongs to one of the three graph families enumerated earlier in the paper.
This empirically observed inequality is presented as a strengthening of the symmetric Laplacian Spread Conjecture; its status is unresolved in the source.
object.source_name: Wayne Barrett, Emily Evans, H. Tracy Hall and Mark Kempton, “New conjectures on algebraic connectivity and the Laplacian spread of graphs”, arXiv:2201.04225 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.04225

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: Weighted Laplacian Spread Conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a weighted graph on $n$ vertices in which every edge weight lies in $[0,1]$, and let $G^c$ be its weighted complement, obtained by replacing each edge weight $w_{ij}$ by $1-w_{ij}$. The algebraic connectivity of a weighted graph is denoted by $\lambda_2$.

**Weighted Laplacian Spread Conjecture.** One has

$$
\lambda_2(G)+\lambda_2(G^c)\geq 1.
$$

This is the natural extension of the symmetric formulation of the Laplacian Spread Conjecture from simple graphs to weighted graphs; the paper reports supporting investigations but no resolution.
object.source_name: Wayne Barrett, Emily Evans, H. Tracy Hall and Mark Kempton, “New conjectures on algebraic connectivity and the Laplacian spread of graphs”, arXiv:2201.04225 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.04225

object.title: Combinatorial positivity conjecture for the Gaussian product inequality
object.statement:
Let $m_2\geq 2$ and $m_3\in\mathbb{N}$. Let $c^{m_2,m_3}_p$ denote the coefficients introduced in the paper's combinatorial formulation of the three-dimensional Gaussian product inequality.

**Combinatorial positivity conjecture.**

$$
c^{m_2,m_3}_p>0\qquad\text{for }3\leq p\leq 2m_2-1.
$$

This coefficient-positivity claim is intended to imply the corresponding three-dimensional Gaussian product inequality. The source verifies related coefficient properties and small cases, but the stated range remains open there.
object.source_name: Oliver Russell and Wei Sun, “Some New Gaussian Product Inequalities”, arXiv:2201.04242 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.04242

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2022). “The GPI conjecture is still open.”

object.title: The analytic torsion formula for three-dimensional spheres
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-sphere, with $f_2(S_i)$ denoting the number of $2$-faces in the unit sphere $S_i$ of a vertex and $f_0(G)$ the number of vertices of $G$. **The analytic torsion formula.**

$$
A(G) = \prod_{i=0}^m f_2(S_i)/(m f_0(G)).
$$

The surrounding discussion relates $A(G)$ to Hodge and Dirac determinants and to spanning-tree counts, but does not establish this formula or clarify the indexing and meaning of $m$ sufficiently.
object.source_name: Oliver Knill, “Analytic torsion for graphs”, arXiv:2201.09412 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09412

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

object.title: Ranked Grothendieck support conjecture
object.statement: Let $w\in S_n$, and let $\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ be the set of exponent vectors of the nonzero terms of $\mathfrak{G}_w$. For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}^n$, compare vectors componentwise, writing $\alpha<\beta$ for strict comparison. **Ranked Grothendieck support conjecture.** If $\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ and $|\alpha|<\deg\mathfrak{G}_w$, then there exists $\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w)$ with $\alpha<\beta$ and $|\beta|=|\alpha|+1$. This is presented as a strengthening of the preceding conjecture and is proved in the paper for Grassmannian permutations; it remains open in general.
object.source_name: Karola Mészáros, Linus Setiabrata and Avery St. Dizier, “On the support of Grothendieck polynomials”, arXiv:2201.09452 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.09452

object.title: The cone-type minimality conjecture for spherical triangulations
object.statement:
Let $\tau$ be a spherical triangulation whose vertices have degree $5$ or $6$. A cycle in $\tau$ is **bad** if it has length $l$ and separates two vertices of degree greater than $l$ in $\tau$. A **cone-type triangulation** at a vertex $v$ is a triangulation in which every tetrahedron contains $v$ and a face in $\tau$. Let $\mathcal{T}^+_n$ and $\mathcal{T}^-_n$ be the triangulations associated with the construction in the paper.

**Cone-type minimality conjecture.** If $\tau$ has no bad cycle, then the cone-type triangulation at a degree-$6$ vertex is minimal, and

$$
\operatorname{flip}(\mathcal{T}^+_n,\mathcal{T}^-_n)=2n-10.
$$

This conjecture would identify a combinatorial condition guaranteeing minimality of the cone-type tetrahedral decomposition and would produce pairs realizing the stated flip distance. No resolution is given in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Zili Wang, “Flip Distance and Triangulations of a Ball”, arXiv:2205.11623 (2022).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.11623

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2022).

object.title: Maillet's conjecture on even numbers as differences of primes
object.statement: Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the set of primes. An even number is an element of $2\mathbb{N}$. **Maillet's conjecture.** Every even number is the difference of two primes. This is a foundational difference-of-primes conjecture and is weaker than the stronger conjectures of Kronecker and Polignac described subsequently; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Sayan Goswami, “Multiplicative largeness of de Polignac numbers”, arXiv:2406.02243 (2024).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1206.0149](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.0149).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02243

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

object.title: Rado-number formula for ${\cal E}(3,0;a,a,b)$
object.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be coprime positive integers, with $a$ odd, and suppose that

$$
3\leq a<b\leq 2a-1.
$$

**Rado-number formula.** Then

$$
R_3({\cal E}(3,0;a,a,b))=a^3b.
$$

The conjecture is based on computational data for Rado numbers of the equation ${\cal E}(3,0;a,a,b)$; no proof or resolution is supplied in the source.
object.source_name: Tanbir Ahmed, Lamina Zaman and Curtis Bright, “Symbolic Sets for Proving Bounds on Rado Numbers”, arXiv:2505.12085 (2025).
object.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1908.11516](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11516), [arXiv:1206.4885](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.4885).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.12085

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

object.title: Nabutovsky's unbounded balanced-vertex conjecture for geodesic nets
object.statement:
A **geodesic net** is a finite embedded graph in the Euclidean plane whose edges are geodesic segments; its vertices are called **unbalanced** or **balanced** according to whether the incident edge directions fail or satisfy the balancing condition. The boundary vertices are the unbalanced vertices.

**Nabutovsky's conjecture.** There exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with $4$ unbalanced vertices and an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. Moreover, this may already hold when the unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square.

This conjecture asks whether the number of balanced vertices can be unbounded when there are four boundary vertices. The paper constructs an irreducible example with $25$ balanced vertices, improving the previous record of $16$, but does not establish arbitrarily large numbers.
object.source_name: Fabian Parsch and Hanrui Zhang, “Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices”, arXiv:2511.07810 (2025).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1803.03728](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03728).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07810

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).
